issues.description: Returning bare nil from run() when leader panicked just relocates the nil-deref one frame up.
issues.detail: When CAS fails and t.result.Load() is nil, run() returns nil. Every caller dereferences the returned *result (output.done, output.Fatal, output.Value). The fix swaps one nil-deref for another. Synthesize a failed-result sentinel with output.Fatal set instead of returning nil, and enforce the postcondition that run() never returns nil.

issues.description: Race window remains open between CAS-fail and Load of t.result.
issues.detail: The fix narrows but does not close the time-of-check/time-of-use window. The leader can still panic and clear t.result between the failed CAS and the subsequent Load. The underlying protocol overloads one atomic pointer's nil/non-nil distinction to encode multiple states, so the same class of bug can recur. Represent 'leader abandoned' explicitly.

issues.description: Comment 'Leader panicked but we did see a result' is the inverse of what the code does.
issues.detail: The branch is taken precisely when we did NOT see a result, but the comment claims we did. This is a typo that inverts intent and will mislead the next maintainer about which branch is which. Fix the comment and write down the actual invariant for the panic path.

issues.description: No regression test exercises the panicking-leader race the PR claims to fix.
issues.detail: The commit message describes a specific race (leader panics, sets result to nil, waiter dereferences), but the diff adds no test that injects a panicking query with concurrent waiters and asserts no nil-deref. Prose in the PR description is not a regression suite. Add a harness that panics the leader and asserts waiters receive a propagated error.

issues.description: t.result is overloaded to encode unclaimed, in-flight, and abandoned states through one nil/non-nil distinction.
issues.detail: The race exists because three identities share one place: leader-election token, result handle, and liveness signal. A small state value or an explicit sentinel for 'abandoned' would make the time semantics explicit instead of inferred from a second Load. This is the root shape that keeps producing nil-deref bugs.

issues.description: checkCycle walks caller.path twice to build a list it already traversed once.
issues.detail: The extracted checkCycle walks the path to find the match, then re-walks from the head to collect nodes up to the match. The extraction is a readability win, but one pass that accumulates and trims (or builds then slices) expresses the computation directly at the same line count. Also missing a stated loop invariant.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges: the PR identifies a real nil-deref race but the fix is incomplete and introduces a new failure mode. Returning bare nil from run() just relocates the crash one frame up, since every caller dereferences the returned *result — synthesize a failed-result sentinel instead. The race window between CAS-fail and the second Load is narrowed but not closed, because t.result is overloaded to encode three distinct states through one atomic pointer. A comment typo inverts the intent of the panic branch, and no regression test reproduces the panicking-leader scenario the commit message describes. NEEDS-WORK before merge.
